column3: “My mouth has opened wide over my enemies” is rendered “My mouth speaks boldly against my enemies.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The doubled “haughty, haughty” becomes “so very proudly”; “a God of knowledge” keeps the Hebrew plural sense as a singular.
Close to the Hebrew; “those who stumble” is rendered “the feeble.”
NASB supplies “to hunger” after “cease” and “children” after “many.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“A throne of honor he makes them inherit” is rendered “inherit a seat of honor.”
“His faithful ones” is rendered “His godly ones.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB makes the Lord the stated object of “those who contend.”
“The lad was serving the LORD” is rendered “the boy ministered to the LORD.”
“Sons of worthlessness” is rendered “worthless men.” NASB carries the sentence into verse 13 (“...the LORD and the custom of the priests”).
NASB links “the custom of the priests” to verse 12’s “did not know”; the Hebrew begins a new statement here. “The fork of three prongs” becomes “a three-pronged fork.”
“All Israel” is rendered “all the Israelites.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “first” and “then,” and turns the scene into a conditional (“if the man said … then he would say”).
Close to the Hebrew.
“Girded with a linen ephod” is rendered “wearing a linen ephod.”
“From days to days” becomes “from year to year,” and “the sacrifice of the days” becomes “the yearly sacrifice.”
“In place of the petition which was asked” is rendered “in place of the one she dedicated”; “his place” becomes “their own home.”
NASB omits the opening “for”; “with the LORD” is rendered “before the LORD.”
Close to the Hebrew.

Close to the Hebrew; the word order is rearranged around “the report.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB uses “can intercede” for the simple future.
“Was going and growing up and good” is rendered “growing in stature and in favor.”
NASB supplies “in bondage” and renders the question as “Did I not indeed reveal Myself…?”
The Hebrew is a statement (“and I chose him”); NASB turns it into a question (“did I not choose them”) and uses plurals (“them,” “My priests”).
“Which I commanded, a dwelling” is rendered “commanded in My dwelling”; the Hebrew is difficult and the meaning is uncertain. “You honor” is singular in Hebrew; NASB keeps the address to Eli.
Close to the Hebrew; “will be insignificant” is rendered “will be lightly esteemed.”
